question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit outbound recipient allowlist for Slack message sends now, and should that policy be Slack-specific or a shared human-chat outbound target policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public config and security semantics under the trusted-operator model, so automation should not choose the product boundary.

options.title: Add shared outbound target policy
options.body: Add an allowTo/allowSendTo-style policy at the shared outbound/channel boundary with Slack schema, docs, and tests while preserving inbound `allowFrom` semantics.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Track Slack recipient gating under the broader outbound guardrails and verified-delivery design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87870.

options.title: Decline core gating for now
options.body: Keep the trusted-operator model unchanged and document that explicit operator sends are not constrained by `dmPolicy` or `allowFrom`.

recommendation.title: Add shared outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Add an allowTo/allowSendTo-style policy at the shared outbound/channel boundary with Slack schema, docs, and tests while preserving inbound `allowFrom` semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The open decision is about product/security config semantics, and history points to steipete on outbound policy and Slack config ownership.
